governance_rationale: Georgia classifies as unitary-small: (1) population ~3.7-3.9M (2014 census 3,713,804; 2024 census 3,929,581) — far below the 20-25M threshold for unitary-large; (2) a single de jure official state language (Georgian; Abkhazian is co-official only within the breakaway Autonomous Republic of Abkhazia, out of government control) so no officially-recognized multi-region minority-language mosaic drives region-level splitting; (3) no widely-recognized internally-split regional identity for the whole country — the historic regions (Kakheti, Imereti, etc.) are cultural, not the basis for distinct geographic governance content. Confirmed as unitary-small with a single WHOLE region (matches DESIGN.md's own example listing).

official_language_legal_source.name: Constitution of Georgia, Article 2(3) (State symbols); and Constitutional/Organic Law of Georgia on the State Language (No 1324 of 13 October 2017)
official_language_legal_source.publisher: Parliament of Georgia / Legislative Herald of Georgia (matsne.gov.ge)
official_language_legal_source.note: The official (state) language of Georgia is Georgian (Kartvelian language, written in the unique Mkhedruli script). Abkhazian is additionally official within the Autonomous Republic of Abkhazia, and Ossetian is de facto used in South Ossetia (Tskhinvali region) — both territories are Russian-occupied / breakaway and outside the Georgian government's control, so only Georgian is official across government-controlled territory.

timezone.note: Georgia abolished daylight saving time in 2005 (last transition 27 March 2005 / final set-back October 2005); UTC+4 year-round since. De facto: the breakaway/occupied regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia follow Moscow Time (UTC+3).

legal_constraints.topic: Not an EU member — EU consumer law does not directly apply
legal_constraints.description: Georgia is a candidate country (candidate status Dec 2023) but NOT an EU member. Therefore the EU's directly-applicable rules (GDPR, Directive 98/6/EC VAT-inclusive price display, Directive 2011/83/EU 14-day withdrawal right, Directive 2019/771 2-year guarantee) do NOT apply as EU law. Consumer protection is governed by Georgian national law (Civil Code, Law on Consumer Rights Protection). Do not copy the EU legal-constraints block used for EU-member files.

The breakaway territories of Abkhazia and South Ossetia (Tskhinvali region) are not under the control of the Georgian government (Russian-occupied); Georgian law, currency and e-commerce do not reliably reach them. Flag for any GEO-wide claim.

popularMethods: Visa and Mastercard bank cards (dominant networks; no domestic card scheme)
Contactless debit/credit cards and mobile wallet apps (TBC, Bank of Georgia apps)
GIPS — NBG instant payment system (2021): real-time 24/7 interbank GEL transfers by phone/account
Cash — still significant in rural areas, bazaars, small towns, and informal/tourism cash economy; common for high-value card transactions by volume
payment_culture.note: Tbilisi and Batumi are strongly cashless-friendly; rural communities and the elderly remain more cash-dependent. Cash remains common at markets and for small informal purchases.

communication_style.summary: Hospitality (stumartmokvareoba) is a core national value: guests are treated as a gift from God. Business is relationship-first — personal trust, reputation (namusi/dignity) and hierarchy matter as much as contracts. Communication is warm, expressive and often indirect (a polite 'yes'/'maybe' may mean 'no'); direct eye contact signals sincerity. The supra (traditional Georgian feast) with a tamada (toastmaster) leading toasts is central to building trust and sealing deals.
communication_style.greetingNorms: Firm handshake with direct eye contact; learn 'gamarjoba' (hello). Respect hierarchy and titles; greet senior/elder people first.
communication_style.meetingEtiquette: Meetings start with social small talk (family, tea/coffee) before business; decisions come from the top of the hierarchy, so include the decision-maker. Punctuality is appreciated but Georgian counterparts may arrive late — not a sign of disrespect.
communication_style.toastsEtiquette: Never toast with beer (used to toast enemies); use wine. When given a toast (alaverdi), elaborate then drink. Refusing a meal invitation is a social misstep.
communication_style.topicsToAvoid: None strongly taboo; personal questions (age, salary, family) are normal small talk.
communication_style.giftGivingNotes: Bringing a small gift (wine, sweets, fruit, flowers) when visiting a home is expected; never arrive empty-handed.
communication_style.sources: trade.gov Country Commercial Guide (Georgia Business Travel); commisceo-global Georgia business culture; georgiaexpats culture & etiquette guide.

climates.description: Humid subtropical — Black Sea west (Adjara/Colchis lowlands incl. Batumi), mild winters, warm humid summers, very heavy rainfall (Batumi ~2,500mm/yr)
Humid continental — eastern plains (Tbilisi, Kakheti): hot dry summers (30-40°C) and cold winters (1-8°C), moderate rainfall
Semi-arid steppe — rain-shadowed Kura river valley / Iori plateau east of the Likhi range
Alpine/mountain — Greater Caucasus (Svaneti, Kazbegi/Gudauri): short cool summers, heavy winter snow

culturalTraits: Supra — the traditional Georgian feast, a multi-hour celebration of food, wine and toasts led by a tamada (toastmaster)

Hospitality (stumartmokvareoba) — the guest is a gift from God
Georgian polyphonic singing and folk dance (UNESCO intangible heritage)
One of the first states to adopt Christianity as state religion (337)
prideOf: Independence and resilience (1991 from USSR; first to defy the USSR)

Tbilisi New Year celebrations (tastes and markets)

businessRhythm.notes: No strict Sunday-trading restriction in law; shops, markets and malls commonly open 7 days (grocery markets often from early morning; malls ~10:00-21:00). State holidays include Independence Day (26 May).
businessRhythm.typicalWorkHours: Standard office hours ~9:00/10:00-18:00/19:00, Mon-Fri; senior staff often start later and work into the evening.

season_notes: Temperate four-season climate. West (Black Sea) is subtropical: mild rainy winters, warm humid summers. East is continental: hot dry summers, cold winters. Mountains are alpine/snowy. Spring (Mar-May) variable; Summer (Jun-Aug) hot, best for coast; Autumn (Sep-Nov) mild, wine harvest (rtveli); Winter (Dec-Feb) cold, good for Tbilisi culture and mountain skiing.
